Apollo Global Management (NYSE:APO) says its private credit trading desk has now traded more than $42 billion in private credit assets since launching earlier this month, up from the $35 billion reported earlier.

John Cortese, partner and co-head of corporate credit at Apollo, told Bloomberg the desk has traded about 620 assets with 185 counterparties. Roughly one-third of that volume involved loans originated by other firms, a share that has held steady since the desk opened.

The desk also added a second trading session in Asia, extending the window in which private credit positions can be bought and sold. Apollo said the expansion is a direct response to demand from investors who want to adjust exposure outside U.S. trading hours.

Apollo Pushes Into Private-Credit Trading

Apollo has rolled out daily marks across its approximately $850 billion credit business. The company says the trading activity is intended to bring more liquidity and price transparency to a market that has historically relied on quarterly valuations.

Cortese said that a growing number of institutional investors are asking for regular pricing on private credit holdings, and that the desk plans to publish aggregate trade data every month starting in November.

The SEC's recent statement on private asset valuations has not slowed the desk's activity, Cortese said, adding that Apollo has already adjusted its internal valuation process to match the regulator's guidance on borrower information.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) is now reported to have finalized its $40 billion financing package, with Apollo leading the bank loans and investment-grade debt. The proceeds will be used to purchase Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) chips.

Pimco has formally committed to the financing, according to people familiar with the matter, and the transaction is still expected to close in 2027.
headline: Apollo Says Private Credit Desk Has Traded $42 Billion, Adds Asia Trading Session
summary: Apollo's private credit trading desk has passed $42 billion in volume, and the firm has added an Asia trading session and plans monthly trade data.
